identity.resolvedIdentity: Elingaard manor, the protected 1749 main building on a medieval noble estate with seventeenth-century cellars, bastions, moats, gardens and a larger cultural landscape.
identity.identityProblem: The place combines a standing manor house, fortified platform, gardens, archaeological landscape, museum functions, rental use and a much larger historical estate. Canonical must identify the main building without treating the whole landscape or visitor address as one geometry.
identity.splitReason: The main building and estate components form one manor place, but the building, park, fortifications, landscape and operational uses require separate anchors and access rules.

requiredEvidence: official address and current museum identity
current tour, rental, park and cultural-trail access controls
separation of building, fortifications and wider cultural landscape

evidence.finding: The named manor-house geometry has a representative coordinate at approximately 59.25222, 10.80250.
evidence.reason: Direct geometry for the standing main building.

evidence.finding: Q5361129 identifies Elingaard as a manor house, cultural property and museum at 59°15′08″N, 10°48′09″E with Kulturminne ID 86064 and OSM way 519150231.
evidence.reason: Provides matching independent entity, coordinate and identifiers.

evidence.finding: The heritage identifier controls the protected manor-house identity and prevents confusion with one garden or landscape component.
evidence.reason: Heritage identity is linked to the same manor entity and OSM geometry.

evidence.finding: Documents the medieval noble-estate roots, seventeenth-century cellars, fires in 1645 and 1746, current 1749 building, noble-family continuity, bankruptcy in 1778, protection in 1923, museum use from 1975, bastions, moats, garden and cultural landscape.
evidence.reason: Authoritative identity, chronology and component source.

evidence.finding: Confirms Elingårdsveien 33, Gressvik as the current visitor address and Østfoldmuseene as the operator.
evidence.reason: Current address and institution control, not replacement building geometry.

evidence.finding: Documents current rental, accommodation and guided-tour functions, and states that museum rooms otherwise remain closed to renters unless included in a guided visit.
evidence.reason: Defines operational access limits for interiors.

evidence.finding: Describes the park, garden and nature-and-culture trail as outdoor visitor areas and identifies the water system, burial field and mill pond as wider landscape components.
evidence.reason: Supports outdoor access while separating landscape from the main-building anchor.

evidence.finding: Gives an independent coordinate at 59.25228, 10.80256, within a few metres of the applied main-building point.
Documents Libertas use of Elingaard as a course centre from 1948 to 1975 and confirms active historical research at the site in June 2026.
evidence.reason: Supports the twentieth-century institutional layer and current museum activity.

evidence.finding: Documents the planned 2025-2026 automatic fire-protection project for the entire main building and its sensitive interiors.
evidence.reason: Supports conservation and temporary-access caution without asserting completion.

evidence.finding: The legacy point lies approximately 5025.7 metres south-west of the manor house.
evidence.reason: Rejected because it has no Elingaard entity or source-object contract.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Matching independent entity and coordinate control; OSM provides direct building geometry.
The address is an arrival control, not a substitute for the building geometry.
The larger estate, archaeological sites, park, garden and mill pond are broader than one canonical coordinate.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted building geometry, manor identity, heritage and address controls, historical layers, operational use, outdoor access and conservation limitations.

decision.nextAction: Applied the named Elingaard main-building geometry and continue with nes_lensemuseum.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 5.03 kilometres north-east.
The standing 1749 main building is canonical.
The medieval estate, seventeenth-century cellars, fortifications, gardens and cultural landscape are separate layers or components.
Indoor access follows tours, events, rental and conservation conditions.
The radius is not a building, property, park, garden, museum, event, water, heritage, safety or access boundary.
